raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Split out of the XPU model-enabling PR #35304 so these shared changes are reviewed on
their own. Neither is gated behind any backend.

## Modification

**Encoder embedding truncation preserves the trailing separator** (`managers/`)
Encoder embedding models (BERT / RoBERTa / ModernBERT / NomicBERT) rely on the
trailing `[SEP]`; a plain head-slice on over-length inputs drops it and shifts the
pooled embedding.
- `managers/utils.py`: the auto-truncation helper takes an optional
  `preserve_last_token_id`; re-append it after the head-slice if the input ended with it.
- `managers/scheduler.py`: resolve `sep_token_id` once (only when `not is_generation`)
  and pass it through.
- `managers/tokenizer_manager.py`: same preservation on that truncation path.
Gated on `not is_generation`, so generation models are unaffected.

**MEAN pooling accumulates in fp32** (`layers/pooler.py`)
`pool_hidden_states` took a batch-wide `torch.cumsum` of the packed hidden states in the
model dtype and differenced it per request. In fp16 / bf16 a short request packed after a
long one loses most of its precision: a 9-token request after a 2028-token one pools at
cosine 0.98 (fp16) / 0.74 (bf16) against the exact mean. The cumsum now runs in fp32 and
the result is cast back to the model dtype. This affects every MEAN-pooled embedder (for
example nomic-embed-text) on every device; CLS and LAST pooling are unchanged.
- `test_pooler_score_and_pool.py`: `test_mean_pooling_short_request_after_long_one_in_half_precision`
  fails before the change and passes after (13/13 in the file).

## Accuracy Test

Intel XPU Arc Pro B60 (tp-1):

| Model | Task / Metric | SGLang B60 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 | MTEB SciFact (ndcg@10) | 49.0 |
| BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 | MTEB STSBenchmark | 75.7 |
| nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | MTEB SciFact (ndcg@10) | 68.03 |
| ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2 | MTEB SciFact (ndcg@10) | 67.20 |

Embeddings match their reference (bge/nomic track H200; granite cos 1.0 fp32 vs HF 68.15).
These B60 numbers are from the `[SEP]` change alone.

fp32 MEAN pooling, `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5` on 1x H200 NVL (tp 1, radix cache off):

| Task / Metric | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MTEB SciFact (ndcg@10) | 68.24 | 70.08 (reference 70.28) |
| MTEB STSBenchmark | 84.25 | 84.25 |

nodes.body: Review request: @hnyls2002 @xiezhq-hermann , this is the shared `managers/` change (SEP-preserving truncation, gated on `not is_generation`) split out of #35304 for focused review. cc @mingfeima.

The qk_norm fix here is also needed on plain CUDA with default flags. Since piecewise CUDA graph became the default (#16331, first shipped in v0.5.10), every HunYuan v1 checkpoint with `use_qk_norm: true` fails at startup on NVIDIA GPUs.

**Repro:** `tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B` (`HunYuanDenseV1ForCausalLM`) on SGLang v0.5.10.post1, launched with `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B` and no extra flags. The piecewise CUDA graph warmup fails at `self.o_proj(attn_output)` in `hunyuan.py`:

```
RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (64x128 and 2048x2048)
```

That is 4 warmup tokens × 16 heads, one head wide. It happens on L4 with flashinfer and with triton, and on H100 with fa3, flashinfer and triton.

**Why CUDA hides it only sometimes:** flashinfer and fa3 return `o.view(-1, heads * head_dim)`, which masks the per-head shape of `q`. The piecewise CUDA graph extend path in `radix_attention.py` allocates `output = torch.empty_like(q)`, so the broken shape reaches `o_proj` on every backend. The triton backend also does `empty_like(q)`, so it never masked the bug.

**What we verified on v0.5.10.post1:**
- **Unpatched, default backend, `--disable-piecewise-cuda-graph`:** the model serves correctly. Tested on L4 with flashinfer and on H100 with fa3, on 32 WMT24++ rows each. Prompt token counts match Transformers on every row, and chrF++ is within noise of a direct Transformers decode.
- **This PR's two-line reshape, triton backend, `--disable-piecewise-cuda-graph`:** loads and serves correctly on L4.

Related: #21127, the same crash on HY-MT1.5-7B, was closed as stale without a fix. #21128 was also closed as stale.

The hunyuan.py change is independent of the encoder truncation change. Could it be split into its own PR so it can be reviewed separately? A small startup smoke test on a HunYuan v1 checkpoint (for example Hy-MT2-1.8B) with piecewise CUDA graph on would also guard against regressions. As far as we can tell, no current test loads one.

Thanks for the detailed repro and root cause, that's really helpful.

I've split the qk_norm fix into its own PR: #41160. It carries the two-line reshape plus a startup smoke test that boots `tencent/Hy-MT2-1.8B` with default flags (piecewise CUDA graph on) and runs a short generation, so the warmup crash is guarded on every backend. Your CUDA root cause (the piecewise-graph `empty_like(q)` path in `radix_attention.py`) is folded into the description there.

This PR is now just the encoder SEP-truncation change.
@hnyls2002 @alphabetc1 can you help take a look?

CUDA check on 1x NVIDIA H200 NVL (tp 1), `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, MTEB. Both runs use the same image (`lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261015-a6a8c560`) with the sglang Python source taken from each commit:
- before: merge-base `58f2c923ed`
- after: this PR `39f6c77d4e`

| Task | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SciFact ndcg@10 | 0.5092 | 0.6018 |
| STSBenchmark | 0.7563 | 0.7563 |
| SciFact ndcg@10, `--disable-radix-cache` | 0.6225 | 0.7380 |
| STSBenchmark, `--disable-radix-cache` | 0.8641 | 0.8641 |

- SciFact has passages longer than 512 tokens, which `--allow-auto-truncate` cuts; this PR keeps their `[SEP]`. STSBenchmark sentences are short and never truncated, so it does not change.
- With `--disable-radix-cache`, the after numbers match the reference scores (SciFact 74.04, STSBenchmark 86.42). The radix cache stays on for encoder embedding models, so later requests reuse prefix tokens computed with an earlier prompt. That is a separate issue on main, not related to this PR.

```bash
sglang serve --model-path BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 --tp-size 1 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --trust-remote-code \
  --is-embedding --dtype bfloat16 --allow-auto-truncate --attention-backend triton   # + --disable-radix-cache for the last two rows
```

MTEB `SciFact` / `STSBenchmark` against the server, batch size 16.

-        cumulative_hidden_states = torch.cumsum(hidden_states, dim=0)
